transcript.text: f/f freezer keeps icing up bottom drawer wont shut proper, defrosted it 2wks ago already full of ice again. indesit

If it’s icing up again within 2 weeks and the bottom freezer drawer won’t shut, it’s usually one of these:

1. Blocked/frozen defrost drain – very common. Defrost water can’t drain away, freezes on the freezer floor and builds up under the bottom drawer.
2. Door not sealing properly – warm moist air gets in and turns to ice. A drawer held open by ice can make this rapidly worse.
3. Fault in the automatic defrost system (on a frost-free Indesit) – e.g. defrost heater, sensor/thermostat or control fault. Ice normally builds behind the rear inside freezer panel first, then spreads.

### What to do now
• Switch it off at the plug, empty the freezer and do a full 24–48 hour defrost with both doors open. Two weeks ago it may not have been long enough to melt ice hidden behind the back panel.
• Put towels down; do not chip ice with a knife/screwdriver or use a heat gun. A bowl of warm water in the compartment can speed it up.
• Once fully clear, check the drain hole/channel at the back/bottom of the freezer, if accessible. Flush gently with warm water using a turkey baster/syringe or flexible pipe cleaner. It should drain away rather than pool.
• Clean and inspect the door seals. Look for splits, gaps, or a drawer/food package stopping the door closing. Test with a strip of paper: shut it in the door; it should grip all round.
• Make sure it is level or very slightly tilted backwards, and set the freezer around –18°C. Don’t overpack it or block internal air vents.

### Important clue
If, after a proper full defrost and making sure the door shuts, the ice is back within 1–2 weeks, especially as a thick sheet on the freezer floor or behind the rear panel, it likely needs an engineer for an auto-defrost fault rather than just another defrost.

Have the model number from the rating label (usually inside the fridge compartment or on the side wall) ready when booking Indesit service.

checked the seal, bottom corner of freezer door seal is split about 5cm and the hinge side bottom bit is flattened. paper slides straight out there, grips everywhere else. its level, thermostat on middle, fridge seal fine. its a manual defrost freezer btw not frost free

That seal fault is almost certainly the cause. On a manual-defrost freezer, warm damp kitchen air entering through that 5 cm split/flattened section will freeze onto the floor and around the bottom drawer, then stop the drawer/door closing properly — which makes the icing accelerate.

### Best fix
Replace the freezer-door gasket/seal. A split seal generally won’t recover or seal reliably, and the paper test confirms it is leaking.

You’ll need the exact Indesit model number to get the correct part. It’s usually on a label inside the fridge compartment, sometimes behind/near the salad drawer or on the side wall. Check whether the gasket is:
• Push-fit / removable, or
• Screwed in behind the inner door liner, or
• Foamed/glued into the door (may require a door or engineer repair on some models).

### Before ordering / fitting
1. Do another proper full defrost and dry everything completely.
2. Check the bottom hinge and door alignment:
• With the door shut, look for it sitting low or dropping when opened.
• Tighten accessible hinge screws/bolts if loose.
• If the door is sagging, the hinge may need adjustment or replacement; a new seal alone may not solve a misaligned door.
3. The flattened section can sometimes improve temporarily: warm it gently with a hairdryer on low, keeping it moving and not overheating the plastic, then close the door for a while so it reforms against the cabinet. This will not fix the split, but may reduce icing until the replacement arrives.

Avoid puncturing/chipping the ice and don’t try to glue the split as a permanent repair — it usually doesn’t remain flexible or airtight at freezer temperatures.

Once the gasket is sealing all the way round, the freezer should no longer build up enough ice in two weeks to foul the bottom drawer.
model is IB55532W on the rating plate. door looks straight not sagging. not sure if the seal is push in or screwed, need a closer look. what do i search for to buy one?

Search for:

“Indesit IB55532W freezer door seal”
or
“Indesit IB 55 532 W freezer door gasket”

Also try adding “white” and, if applicable, “lower freezer door gasket”.

The model alone can sometimes cover several production versions, so use the full 12-digit service/commercial code from the rating plate as well — it often begins with 85…. Search or give a parts supplier both, for example:

> Indesit IB55532W freezer door gasket 85xxxxxxxxxx

Don’t buy a “universal magnetic fridge/freezer seal” unless you can confirm the dimensions and fixing method; they are often poor fits.

Before ordering, inspect the seal at an edge/corner:

• Push-fit: the gasket lip pushes into a channel in the door liner; usually removable by gently pulling at an inner edge.
• Screw-fixed: screws are visible under the inner gasket flap; the gasket is clamped by the door liner.
• Foamed-in / non-removable: no visible screws or release channel, and it appears permanently bonded into the door. In that case the seal may not be sold separately, and a repairer may advise a door replacement or a specialist seal repair.

Useful UK parts sites to check with the model and service code are Indesit/Hotpoint spares, eSpares, Partmaster, BuySpares, and Ransom Spares. Check the listing specifically says it fits your full service code, not just “similar Indesit models.”
